description: Out-of-region corner test of the v×C bound (India UPI, Brazil Pix, Kenya M-Pesa). The bound's fate splits by the level at which concentration is measured: app-level bound FALSIFIED (Pix, UPI), rail-level bound survives near-definitionally. The refined conclusion: speed requires a single rail (one stalk); the free choice is the stalk's Heyting backstop — who pays when it fails.

cases.app_level: decentralized (runs in every bank/fintech app; no dominant front-end; exact shares unpublished)

cases.velocity_note: 2016 launch → hundreds of millions of users; ~13B tx/month by 2024-12; clearly fast (≥4pp/yr of adults)
cases.app_level: duopoly: PhonePe 47.7% + Google Pay 36.7% (top app <50%, top-2 ~85%) — borderline
cases.rail_level: concentrated (single NPCI rail carries the bulk of retail digital payments)
sources: NPCI Dec-2024 data via Statista / theheadandtale

cases.velocity_note: 2007 launch → 68.7% of adults with mobile money by 2021 (Findex); historically fast

app_level_bound.detail: Pix: ~67pp/yr with no dominant app; UPI: top app 47.7% (<50).

rail_level_bound.detail: All fast adopters ride a single shared rail (BCB/NPCI/Safaricom/ITMX).

refined_structural_conclusion: v×C is not one claim but two: at the app level it is FALSE (Pix/UPI prove fast+plural front-ends), at the rail level it is TRUE but almost by construction. Fragility therefore cannot be avoided by app plurality — the single stalk remains; the only real choice is its Heyting backstop type (⊤_pub vs consortium vs ⊤_priv), which determines who absorbs the failure. This sharpens Finding 5 and reconnects to the sheaf/single-stalk analysis (notes/25) at the rail level.
honest_limits: Velocity units are not perfectly commensurable across cases (Findex pp/yr for ASEAN vs platform-user growth for Pix/UPI). Pix front-end shares are not centrally published (decentralization inferred from its in-every-bank-app design). UPI top app 47.7% is borderline vs the 50% threshold. Also: the Findex 'mobileaccount' indicator misses UPI/Pix (IND 10.4%, BRA 27.0% in 2021) because they are bank-rail systems — the indicator measures an account TYPE, not the payment function.
